V.2 Map Class Diagram and Interaction Diagram to Code	13
V.2 Applying Service Discovery Pattern in the service-oriented architecture	13

MagiSound is a music streaming website that allows users to search for and listen to public songs online. Guests can browse the music catalog, listen to recommended tracks, and register an account, while registered Users can manage their personal profiles, favorite songs, playlists, and uploaded tracks. Uploaded tracks must be reviewed and assessed by Staff before becoming publicly available. Staff also handles content violation reports and ensures community guidelines, while Admin manages staff accounts, music genres, and views system statistics.

MagiSound stores audio and multimedia files internally within the system database and server storage, uses an Email Service for account verification and password recovery, and relies on SQL Server for relational business data.
FE-01: Account Registration and Email Verification - Allows guests to register a new account with a unique email and verify it via a single-use token.
FE-02: Authentication and Password Recovery - Enables users to log in, log out, and securely reset forgotten passwords via email verification codes.
FE-03: Public Song Catalog - Displays approved public tracks with metadata including title, uploader, genre, and duration.
FE-04: Song Search and Filtering - Allows searching public tracks by keyword and filtering by music genres.
FE-05: Song Streaming - Streams approved audio tracks using HTTP range requests directly from internal server storage.
FE-06: Recommended Songs Discovery - Displays trending and recommended songs on the home page for guests and users.
FE-07: Playback Control - Provides full playback controls including play, pause, seek, next, previous, shuffle, loop, and queue management.
FE-08: Personal Profile Management - Allows users to view and update their profile information, bio, and avatar.
FE-09: Favorite Songs Management - Enables users to add approved tracks to their favorites list and manage their collection.
FE-10: Playlist Management - Allows users to create, update, reorder, and delete personal playlists without affecting catalog tracks.
FE-11: Read-only Track Details and Lyrics - Displays track metadata, artist info, and synchronized or plain text lyrics.
FE-12: Personal Track Management and Upload - Allows users to upload MP3 tracks with metadata for staff review and manage uploaded songs.
FE-13: Track Submission Monitoring - Lets uploaders track review status (Pending, Approved, Rejected) with detailed feedback.
FE-14: Content Violation Report Submission - Allows users to flag inappropriate or copyright-infringing tracks with categories and explanations.
FE-15: Song Submission Moderation - Enables staff to inspect metadata, listen to audio files, and approve or reject submitted tracks.
FE-16: Content Report Resolution and Takedown - Enables staff to review violation reports and remove confirmed violating tracks from the public catalog.
FE-17: Staff Account Management - Allows admin to view staff directory, create staff accounts, and deactivate staff members.
FE-18: Music Genre Management - Allows admin to create, edit, and deactivate music genre categories.
FE-19: System Statistics and Metrics - Displays aggregated metrics on accounts, tracks, moderation queue, and listening activity.
The Context Diagram establishes the boundary of the MagiSound System. The system interacts with 5 external entities:
1. Guest: Unauthenticated visitor who browses catalog, searches songs, plays music, and submits registration.
2. User: Authenticated member who manages playlists, favorites, profile, uploads tracks, and reports violations.
3. Staff: Content moderator who reviews submitted songs, approves or rejects tracks, and resolves violation reports.
4. Admin: System administrator who creates and deactivates staff accounts, manages genres, and views system metrics.
5. Email Service: External secondary service that receives automated dispatch requests and sends verification tokens and reset links.

* Architectural Note: Audio data and multimedia files are stored internally within the system server storage and relational SQL Server database; therefore, Database and Server Storage are internal system components and not external actors.

Automatically connects with the Email Service (Secondary Actor) to send welcome emails upon successful account creation and verification links/codes for password recovery. Additionally, this function automatically dispatches notifications regarding User's track moderation decisions, and account ban warnings.

Applies byte-range data transmission techniques (HTTP Range Requests) to distribute audio streams directly to the User's browser. Since external Cloud Storage is no longer used, this function automatically extracts small data chunks of the MP3 file from the internal server for real-time playback, optimizing bandwidth, minimizing latency, and ensuring smooth track seeking.

Receives, validates (enforcing format standards like MP3, JPG, PNG, WEBP and size limits of 5MB for images, 15MB for audio files), and directly stores multimedia files uploaded by Users onto the system's internal server.

A background process that continuously monitors playback duration. The system automatically logs the listening history and only increments a valid play count when it verifies the User has continuously listened to a track for 30 seconds or more. This data is subsequently aggregated and displayed on the User's statistics dashboard.

Executes backend data logic when a User permanently deletes an Album. The function automatically unlinks the association (sets Album_ID to Null) for all tracks belonging to that Album in the database, seamlessly converting them into standalone Singles without deleting the original audio files.
The user is not logged in. They can browse the music catalog, play public music, log in, register an account, and request to reset a forgotten password.

The user is logged in. They can manage their personal profile, favorites, and playlists, submit content reports, and view read-only lyrics. They also have content creation capabilities to upload tracks for review, view track review results, and manage their own albums.
Content Management Specialist. Responsible for reviewing pending tracks (approving or rejecting them with mandatory reasons) and resolving content reports (including removing violating tracks).
System Admin. Manages user accounts and roles, oversees music genre categories, and views system statistics.
The third-party service (Secondary Actor) automatically sends account registration confirmation emails and password recovery codes.
Figure 1: Use case diagram of Guest
Figure 2: Use case diagram of User
Figure 3: Use case diagram of Staff
Figure 4: Use case diagram of Admin

Creates a new MagiSound account by collecting a unique email address, password, and required registration information. The system validates the submitted data, securely encodes the password, creates the account in a pending-verification state, and requests a verification email.

Verifies the registered email address through a valid, time-limited, single-use token. After successful verification, the system activates the account, marks the email as verified, and invalidates the verification token.

Authenticates an actor using an email address and password. The system verifies the credentials, email-verification status, account status, and assigned fixed system role before creating an authenticated session and redirecting the actor to an authorized page.

Retrieves and displays approved public songs and albums. The catalog provides summary information such as song title, uploader, genre, album, cover image, and duration, and allows the actor to open a selected item's details.

Searches approved public songs, albums, and uploaders using a keyword. The actor may filter the results by genre or content type, and the system displays only content that is approved and publicly available.

Streams an approved public song and provides playback controls, including play, pause, seek, next, previous, and volume adjustment. The system updates the player state and may record a listening event when the valid-play condition is satisfied.

Retrieves and displays the official lyrics available for the selected song in read-only form. If no lyrics are available, the system displays an informative empty state. Creating, editing, translating, or switching custom lyric versions is not supported.

Ends the current authenticated session by invalidating the session or authentication token, clearing local authentication data, and redirecting the actor to a public page. Protected functions require a new login after logout.

Allows a Guest who has forgotten a password to request a time-limited reset link by email. The system validates the reset token and password policy, securely stores the new password, invalidates the token, and redirects the Guest to Login.
Create: Submits a new report for an existing public song by
selecting a report category and entering a description. The report is stored with a Pending status for Staff review.

Read: Displays the User's submitted reports, including the reported song, category, submission date, current status, and resolution information when available. Users cannot update or delete a submitted report.
Create: Creates a new playlist with a name, description, visibility, and optional cover information.
Read: Displays the User's playlists and the songs contained in each playlist.
Update: Changes playlist information, adds available songs, removes songs, changes song positions, and updates visibility.
Delete: Deletes an owned playlist and its playlist-song relationships without deleting the original songs.
Create: Creates a personal album using a title, description, cover information, and release information.
Read: Displays albums owned by the User and the songs organized in each album.
Update: Changes album information, adds owned songs, or removes songs from an album.
Delete: Deletes the selected album and its album-song relationships without deleting the original song records.
Create: Adds an approved public song to the User's favorites collection while preventing duplicate favorite records.
Read: Displays all currently available songs in the User's favorites collection.
Delete: Removes the selected song from Favorites without deleting the original song. An Update operation is unnecessary because a favorite relationship has no editable information.

Displays the review results of songs uploaded by the authenticated User. The system shows each submission as Pending, Approved, or Rejected and displays the Staff rejection reason when the submission has been rejected. Review results are read-only for the User.
Read: Displays the personal profile associated with the authenticated account.

Update: Allows the User to modify permitted profile fields such as username, display name, biography, avatar, date of birth, and country. The system validates the information and preserves the previous profile if saving fails. Profile creation and deletion are not provided because the profile belongs to the registered account.

Uploads a supported audio file together with required song metadata such as title, genre, description, album information, and cover information. The system validates and stores the audio and metadata, creates the song with a Pending status, and places it in the Staff review queue. The song is not publicly available before approval.

Retrieves the queue of Pending song submissions and allows Staff to select a submission, inspect its uploader and metadata, and listen to its audio. After completing the assessment, Staff may approve or reject the submission.

Approves a reviewed Pending song that satisfies content, metadata, and audio-quality requirements. The system changes its status to Approved, records the reviewer and review time, and makes the song eligible to appear in the public catalog.

Rejects a reviewed Pending song that violates content rules or does not satisfy metadata or audio-quality requirements. The system changes its status to Rejected and prevents it from becoming publicly available.

Requires Staff to enter a non-empty reason before a song rejection can be completed. The system validates and stores the reason with the review result so that the uploader can understand why the submission was rejected.

Retrieves Pending content reports and allows Staff to inspect the report category, description, reporter information, and reported song. Staff may listen to the song and review its metadata before determining whether the report is valid.

Records the final decision for a reviewed content report. If the report is invalid, the system rejects and closes it without changing the song. If the report is valid, the system records the resolution and allows the violating song to be removed from public access.

Removes a song that has been confirmed to violate content rules from the public catalog, search results, public albums, and playback. The system records the removal reason and uses a recoverable status such as Removed or Unavailable instead of immediately deleting the stored audio.
Read: Searches and displays registered accounts and their profile and status information.

Update: Locks an account to prevent authenticated access or unlocks a previously locked account. Admin cannot create accounts because account creation is handled by Register, cannot assign roles because dynamic role management is outside the project scope, and cannot permanently delete accounts through this use case.
Create: Creates a new music genre with a unique name, slug, description, and active status.
Read: Displays all genres and their current status.
Update: Changes genre information or activates and deactivates a genre.
Delete: Deletes a genre only when it is not referenced by any song; a referenced genre must be deactivated instead of deleted.

Aggregates and displays basic system statistics, including the number of accounts, active and locked accounts, songs, Pending, Approved and Rejected submissions, content reports, and listening activity. This use case is read-only and does not modify source data; advanced analytics are outside the project scope.

Creates a new MagiSound account by collecting a unique email address, display name, and password. The system validates submitted data, hashes the password, creates the account in a Pending status, and requests Email Service to send a verification token.
PRE-1. Guest is not logged into the system.
PRE-2. Guest provides an accessible, valid email address.
POST-1. A new account record is created with status "Pending_Verification".
POST-2. A single-use verification token is created and sent via Email Service.
2. Guest enters email, display name, password, and password confirmation.
4. System validates email syntax and checks email uniqueness.
5. System validates password meets minimum 8 characters and complexity.
8. System creates new User account with status "Pending_Verification".
9. System invokes UC-02 to generate verification token and dispatch email.
10. System notifies Guest to verify email address.
AF-1. Email already registered: System displays "Email already in use" and prompts login.
AF-. Password policy violated: System displays error detailing password requirements.
E-1. The email is already registered; the system rejects the request and displays an error.
E-2. The input is invalid; the system identifies the invalid fields.
E-3. The verification email cannot be sent; the account remains pending and the system allows the email to be resent later.
The Guest provides truthful and accessible registration information.
The Guest opens the verification link received by email.
The system validates the verification token and activates the corresponding pending account.
PRE-2. A verification token has been issued for the account.
POST-1. The account email is marked as verified.
POST-2. The account becomes eligible to log in.
POST-3. The token is marked as used.
1. The Email Service delivers the verification message.
2. The Guest opens the verification link.
4. The system activates the account and invalidates the token.
5. The system displays a successful verification message.
AF-1. If the account is already verified, the system displays that no further verification is required.
AF-2. The Guest requests a new verification email; the system invalidates the previous active token and issues a new one.
E-1. The token is invalid, expired, or already used; the system refuses activation and provides a resend option.
E-2. The account no longer exists; the system displays an invalid request message.
Once for each newly registered account, with occasional retries.
Token validation and account activation must be completed consistently in one transaction.
The Guest can access the registered email inbox.
The actor submits the login form.
The system authenticates the account and grants access according to its active role.
PRE-1. The actor is not authenticated.
POST-1. A valid authenticated session is established.
POST-2. The actor is redirected to an authorized page.
1. The actor opens the login page.
2. The actor enters an email address and password.
3. The system validates the credentials and account status.
4, The system creates an authenticated session.
5. The system redirects the actor based on the assigned role.
AF-1. The actor selects Forgot Password; the system starts UC-04.
E-1. The credentials are incorrect; the system displays a generic authentication error.
E-2. The email is not verified; the system denies access and offers to resend verification.
E-3. The account is locked; the system denies access and displays the account status.
Authentication errors must not reveal whether a specific email address exists.
The actor remembers valid credentials or can access the reset-password function.
Actor clicks "Forgot Password?" link on Login page.
Allows an actor who forgot their password to request a password reset code via email, verify identity, and securely set a new password
PRE-1. Account exists with a registered and verified email address.
PRE-2. Account is not banned or deactivated
POST-1. Password reset token is generated and delivered via Email Service.
POST-2. Account password is updated to the newly provided hashed password.
POST-3. Reset token is consumed; existing sessions are terminated.
1. Actor clicks "Forgot Password?" on Login page.
2. Actor inputs registered email address and submits.
3. System verifies email exists and account is active.
4. System invokes UC-02 to generate password reset token (15 min TTL) and dispatch email.
5. System displays notification instructing Actor to check email for reset link/code.
6. Actor opens email and clicks reset link.
7. System validates token via UC-02 and presents New Password form.
8. Actor enters new password and confirms new password.
9. System validates new password against complexity policy (BR-02).
10. System hashes new password with BCrypt, updates database, and invalidates reset token.
11. System displays success message and redirects Actor to Login page.
AF-1. Email not found: System displays generic message "If your email is registered, you will receive a reset link" (prevents email enumeration).
AF-2. Password policy violated: System prompts Actor with policy requirements.
E-1. Token expired or invalid: System displays "Password reset link has expired. Please request a new one.".
Actor clicks "Log Out" button on navigation bar or profile menu.
Terminates active authenticated session, invalidates session token, and redirects Actor to public home page.
PRE-1. Actor is currently authenticated with a valid session.
POST-1. Session cookie/token is deleted on client and invalidated on server.
POST-2. Actor is redirected to public Home page as Guest.
1. Actor clicks "Log Out" on navigation bar.
2. System receives logout request and extracts session token.
3. System invalidates server-side session / adds JWT token to revocation list.
4. System clears authentication cookies and client local storage.
5. System redirects Actor to public Home page.
E-1. Network error during logout: Client forces local credential purge and redirects to Home page.
Client-side storage is accessible for clearing.
Actor opens the MagiSound Home page or Explore page.
Displays curated, trending, and newly approved public tracks on the home discovery page to help guests and users discover popular music.
PRE-2. System contains approved public tracks in the database.
POST-1. Curated list of recommended and trending tracks is displayed with cover, title, artist, genre, and duration.
1. Actor navigates to MagiSound Home / Explore page.
2. System queries database for approved tracks sorted by play count, recent approval date, and genre popularity.
3. System filters out non-approved or taken-down tracks.
4. System renders categorized carousels: "Trending Now", "New Releases", "Popular Genres".
5. Actor scrolls through recommendations, clicks track card to view details.
AF-1. Database contains fewer than 5 tracks: System displays available tracks and a welcome banner inviting users to upload music.
E-1. Database query error: System renders placeholder layout and displays "Unable to load recommendations. Please refresh."
Track metadata and cover image URLs are properly indexed.
Actor enters keywords in the search bar or selects a genre filter.
Allows guests and users to search the public catalog of approved songs by track title, artist name, or lyrics keywords, and filter results by music genre.
PRE-2. Only tracks with status "Approved" and availability "Public" are queried.
POST-1. Matching search and filter results are displayed in a paginated list.
1. Actor enters search query into search bar or selects a genre from dropdown filter.
2. System captures search input (minimum 1 character) and active genre filter.
3. System executes full-text search against approved track titles, artists, and lyrics.
4. System filters results matching the selected genre (if applicable).
5. System returns matching tracks sorted by relevance or play count.
6. System displays list with track cover, title, artist, genre, duration, and play button.
AF-1. No matching tracks found: System displays "No songs found matching your keyword. Explore trending songs below."
E-1. Database search timeout: System returns "Search service busy. Please try a simpler keyword."
Special characters in search input are sanitized against SQL injection.
Actor clicks on a track title, cover, or "View Details" button.
Displays complete metadata of an approved track, including title, artist/uploader, genre, release date, play count, description, and read-only lyrics.
PRE-1. Target track exists and has "Approved" status.
POST-1. Track detail modal or dedicated track page is rendered. No data is modified.
1. Actor clicks on a track card or row from catalog, search, or playlist.
2. System retrieves track record, artist profile, genre name, and associated lyrics from database.
3. System formats playback duration and total play count.
4. System displays Track Details view showing cover art, title, artist, genre, release date, play count, and official lyrics.
5. Actor reads lyrics, views metadata, or clicks "Play" to start streaming.
AF-1. Track has no lyrics submitted: System displays metadata and shows note "Lyrics have not been submitted for this track yet."
E-1. Track not found or was removed: System displays "Track is no longer available" and redirects to catalog.
Lyrics are stored as UTF-8 formatted text.
Actor clicks "Play" button on any track card, row, or detail view.
Initiates audio playback of an approved public song using byte-range streaming directly from the system internal server storage, and triggers play count tracking.
PRE-1. Target track has status "Approved" and audio file exists in internal server storage.
PRE-2. Actor client browser supports HTML5 Audio and HTTP Range Requests.
POST-1. Audio stream begins playing in persistent player.
POST-2. Track is set as current playing track in queue.
POST-3. Play Count and History Tracker monitors playback to record valid play (>30s).
1. Actor clicks "Play" button on a track.
2. System verifies track is approved and accessible.
3. System sends initial byte-range audio chunk from internal server storage to client browser.
4. Client browser begins audio decoding and playback in persistent player bar.
5. System initializes Play Count Tracker timer for the active session.
6. When continuous playback reaches 30 seconds, system increments track play count in database.
7. If Actor is authenticated User, system logs track to User's listening history.
AF-1. Actor clicks "Play All" on playlist: System loads entire playlist into playback queue and plays first track.
E-1. Audio file missing or corrupted in internal storage: System displays "Audio unavailable. Error loading audio stream."
E-2. Network disconnection: Browser pauses playback and displays buffer indicator until connection restored.
HTTP Range Requests are handled by backend streaming endpoint.
Actor interacts with controls on the persistent playback bar.
Allows actor to control active audio playback including play, pause, seek progress bar, skip to next/previous track, adjust volume, toggle shuffle, toggle repeat mode, and view current queue.
PRE-1. A track is currently loaded or playing in the persistent player.
POST-1. Player state (position, status, volume, queue sequence) updates immediately according to action.
1. Clicks Pause/Play: System toggles audio playback state.
2. Drags Seek Slider: System sends byte-range request for specified timestamp; audio resumes from new position.
3. Adjusts Volume / Mute: System adjusts audio output gain.
4. Clicks Next Track: System loads and plays next song in queue.
5. Clicks Previous Track: If elapsed > 3s, restarts current song; otherwise plays previous song in queue.
6. Toggles Shuffle: System randomizes queue order.
7. Toggles Repeat: System cycles modes (No Repeat, Repeat All, Repeat One).
8. Clicks Queue: System expands queue panel showing upcoming songs.
AF-1. Next track clicked at end of queue: If Repeat All is ON, loops to first track; if OFF, playback stops.
E-1. Next song in queue unavailable or removed: System skips to subsequent available track.
Persistent player state remains active across page navigation via SPA architecture.
The system terminates the current session and returns the actor to a public page.
POST-1. The current session or authentication token is invalidated.
POST-2. Protected pages require authentication again.
2. The system invalidates the current session.
3. The system clears local authentication data.
4. The system redirects to a public page.
AF-1. The session has already expired; the system clears local authentication data and redirects to Login.
E-1. The server cannot process logout; the client still removes local credentials and requires a new login.
Protected API requests made after logout must be rejected.
The actor uses one active browser session at a time.
User clicks on avatar or selects "My Profile" from account dropdown.
Retrieves and displays profile details of the authenticated user, including avatar, display name, username, email, bio, registration date, and statistics (number of uploaded tracks and playlists)
PRE-1. User is authenticated with an active session.
POST-1. Profile data is displayed to the user. No data is modified.
2. System identifies User_ID from authenticated session token.
3. System queries user profile, account details, uploaded tracks count, and playlist count from database.
4. System renders profile screen with avatar image, display name, username, bio, join date, and statistics cards.
E-1. Profile record not found: System creates default profile linked to account and displays.
Avatar URL points to valid internal storage path or default avatar.
User clicks "Edit Profile" or "Save Changes" on profile page.
Allows authenticated user to update their display name, bio, and upload a new avatar image. Uploaded avatar files are validated and stored in internal server storage.
PRE-2. New avatar image (if provided) is in JPG/PNG/WEBP format and under 5MB.
POST-1. User profile details and avatar path are updated in database.
POST-2. New avatar file is persisted in internal server storage.
1. User enters edit mode on profile page.
2. User updates display name, biography text, and optionally selects a new avatar image file.
4. System validates display name length (2 to 50 characters) and bio length (max 500 characters).
5. If new avatar provided: system validates file format and size (<= 5MB), saves file to internal server storage directory, and generates local file URI.
6. System updates user profile record in database.
7. System displays "Profile updated successfully" message and updates avatar in navigation bar.
AF-1. Display name empty or exceeds limit: System displays validation error.
AF-. Avatar file exceeds 5MB or invalid format: System rejects upload and keeps existing avatar.
E-1. Internal storage write error: System aborts update and informs user to retry.
Images are stored on internal server disk.
User clicks "Heart" icon on a track or navigates to "Favorite Songs" library.
Allows an authenticated user to add or remove approved public tracks to/from their personal favorites collection and browse their liked tracks.
PRE-2. Target track exists and has status "Approved".
POST-1. Track is added to or removed from User's Favorites relation in database.
POST-2. Heart icon toggles visual state (filled vs outlined).
1. User clicks "Heart" (Favorite) icon next to a song in catalog, player, or track details.
2. System checks if track is already in User's favorites list.
3. If not in favorites: System inserts favorite record linking User_ID and Track_ID with timestamp.
4. If already in favorites: System removes favorite record.
5. System returns updated favorite state to client.
6. Client updates Heart icon visually and updates favorite count.
7. (Browse flow): User navigates to "Favorite Songs" page; system queries and displays all tracks favorited by User, sorted by date added.
7a. User has no favorited tracks: System displays empty state "You haven't liked any songs yet. Discover trending tracks!" with link to Explore.
E-1. Target track was deleted or banned: System displays "Song is no longer available" and removes it from favorites list.
Adding to favorites requires an active User session.
User clicks unfilled "Heart" icon on a track row or player bar.
Adds an approved public track to the authenticated user's personal favorites list.
PRE-1. User is authenticated with active session.
PRE-2. Target track is approved and public.
PRE-3. Track is not already in user's favorites list.
POST-1. A new favorite relationship record (User_ID, Track_ID, Created_At) is saved in database.
POST-2. Heart icon toggles to filled active state.
1. User clicks unfilled Heart icon on a track.
2. Client sends add-favorite request with Track_ID to backend.
3. System validates user session and verifies track status is Approved.
4. System checks if favorite already exists; confirms not favorited.
5. System inserts favorite record into database.
7. Client updates Heart icon to filled state and increments track's favorite count.
E-1. Track has been removed or taken down: System alerts "Song is no longer available" and disables action.
User must be signed in to favorite tracks.
User clicks filled "Heart" icon on a previously favorited track.
Removes an existing track from the authenticated user's personal favorites collection.
PRE-2. Target track currently exists in user's favorites list.
POST-1. The favorite record linking User_ID and Track_ID is deleted from database.
POST-2. Heart icon toggles to unfilled inactive state.
1. User clicks filled Heart icon on a track.
2. Client sends remove-favorite request with Track_ID.
3. System verifies user session and locates existing favorite record.
4. System deletes favorite record from database.
6. Client updates Heart icon to unfilled state; if user is on Favorites page, track is removed from view.
E-1. Database deletion error: System informs user and retains previous state.
Removing from favorites does not affect catalog track.
User clicks "Favorite Songs" or "Liked Songs" in navigation menu.
Retrieves and displays all approved public songs favorited by the user, ordered by most recently added.
POST-1. List of favorited tracks is rendered with thumbnail, title, artist, genre, duration, and play action.
1. User navigates to "Favorite Songs" library page.
2. System queries favorites table for User_ID joined with approved tracks table.
3. System filters out any tracks that have been deactivated or taken down
4. System returns list of favorited tracks sorted by date favorited descending.
5. System displays tracks with total count and "Play All" option.
6. User can play songs or remove songs from favorites.
AF-1. User has not favorited any songs: System renders empty state with "No liked songs yet" and a link to explore trending songs.
E-1. Database query error: System displays "Failed to load favorites. Please refresh."
Favorites are private to the owning user.
User clicks "New Playlist" or "Create Playlist" button in library sidebar.
Creates a new, empty playlist owned by the authenticated user with a customizable title and optional description.
PRE-1. User is authenticated with active session .
POST-1. New playlist record is inserted into database linked to User_ID.
POST-2. New playlist appears in user's sidebar playlist list.
2. System generates new playlist with default title "My Playlist #N" owned by User.
3. System saves playlist record with User_ID and creation timestamp.
4. System opens newly created playlist detail view in edit mode.
5. User enters custom playlist name, optional description, and clicks "Save".
6. System validates title length (1 to 100 characters).
7. System updates playlist title and description in database.
8. System displays confirmation and refreshes playlist view.
AF-1. Playlist title is empty: System sets title to default "Untitled Playlist".
E-1. Database insertion failure: System displays "Could not create playlist. Please try again."
User clicks on a playlist name in the library sidebar or navigates to "My Playlists".
Displays playlist header information (title, description, owner, total tracks, total duration) and list of associated tracks in sequenced order.
POST-1. Playlist details and song list are rendered. No data modified.
1. User clicks on a playlist in sidebar.
2. System queries playlist metadata by Playlist_ID and verifies user ownership or public status.
3. System queries joined playlist_tracks table for Track details ordered by sequence index.
4. System filters out tracks that have been removed or taken down (BR-07).
5. System calculates total track count and aggregate duration.
6. System displays playlist header and track rows with cover, title, artist, duration, and play buttons.
AF-1. Playlist contains zero tracks: System displays empty playlist notice with search bar to "Add songs to this playlist".
E-1. Playlist not found: System redirects to library with error "Playlist does not exist."
Playlist tracks point to existing catalog tracks.
User clicks "Edit Details", reorders tracks, or clicks "Add/Remove Song from Playlist".
Allows the playlist owner to update playlist title and description, add approved catalog songs, remove songs, and reorder songs within the playlist.

Provide the business rules those are applied only to the use case
Each account must use a unique valid email address.
A password must meet the configured minimum length and complexity requirements and must be securely encoded before storage.
A newly registered account remains pending and cannot log in until its email is verified.
Email verification and password-reset tokens must expire and may be used only once.
A locked or deleted account cannot log in or use protected functions.
Protected functions require a valid authenticated session with the appropriate role.
Only an Approved and available track may appear in search, the public catalog, albums, or public playback.
A listening event is counted only after the configured valid-play condition is satisfied.
A User may access or modify only personal resources unless the resource is intentionally public.
Username and other configured unique profile identifiers must not duplicate another active profile.
Favorites and playlists must reference existing tracks that are available to the User.
Only the playlist owner may update or delete the playlist and manage its tracks.
Users may view available lyrics but cannot create, edit, translate, or switch custom lyric versions.
A report must reference an existing public track and include a valid category and description.
A submitted track must contain the required metadata and a supported audio file and must initially have Pending status.
The audio data and its track record must be stored consistently; a failed upload must not leave an incomplete public track.
Every Rejected track must have a non-empty rejection reason visible to its uploader.
A User may add only owned tracks to an owned album, and an unapproved track cannot become public through an album.
Only a Pending track may be approved or rejected, and one final review decision is stored for that review cycle.
Staff and Admin operations require the corresponding role.
A content report must record its final decision, resolution note, handler, and handling time.
Only Admin may assign privileged roles, and the system must preserve at least one usable Admin account.
A genre referenced by track data must not be physically deleted; it may be deactivated instead.
System statistics must be aggregated and must not expose passwords, tokens, or unnecessary personal information.
